notes.meaning: David became deeply discouraged and convinced himself that Saul would eventually kill him. Instead of asking God for direction, he chose on his own to run away to the Philistines so Saul would stop chasing him. Even strong believers can struggle with fear and doubt God's promises when hardships drag on.
David gathered his six hundred fighting men and crossed over the border into Philistine territory. He went straight to Achish son of Maoch, the king of the city of Gath, to seek safety.

David and his men settled down in Gath under the protection of Achish. The soldiers brought their families with them, and David brought his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Bringing their households showed Achish that they intended to stay and serve him peacefully.

When Saul heard that David had fled into Philistine territory, he finally stopped hunting for him. David had moved outside the borders of Israel into enemy land where Saul could no longer easily march with his army.

David politely asked King Achish for a place to live in a smaller country town rather than the capital city. Living outside Gath gave David more freedom and helped his men avoid conflicts with the Philistine court.

Achish granted the request and gave David the town of Ziklag, located southwest of Gath. The town had once been assigned to Israel, but the Philistines held it until this time. From then on, Ziklag became the permanent property of the kings of Judah.
David lived in Philistine territory for a full year and four months. This sixteen-month period was a long, spiritually trying season of exile for him among pagan neighbors.

From his base in Ziklag, David led his troops on raids against nomadic groups like the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites. These wandering peoples lived in the southern desert toward Egypt and had long troubled the border towns of Israel.

differ.view: David was carrying out God's ancient judgment against pagan nations long condemned to destruction, finishing the work Saul had left undone.
David acted without any divine command, waging unauthorized and harsh raids to secure plunder and keep his position.
David was acting as a raider fighting for survival and goods rather than God's honor, stepping into a pattern of using violence to protect himself.

notes.meaning: When David attacked these desert groups, he wiped out every man and woman and carried off their livestock and clothing. He gathered this large plunder and returned to King Achish as if he were a faithful vassal.

When Achish asked where David had gone raiding, David gave an answer designed to mislead him. He named areas in southern Judah and allied lands, leading the king to believe he was attacking his own countrymen rather than foreign desert tribes.

David refused to spare any captives to bring back to Gath so no one could report what he had actually done. He kept up this harsh practice the entire time he stayed among the Philistines to keep his real raids secret from the king.

Achish completely believed David's story and thought David had made himself thoroughly hated by his own people in Israel. As a result, the Philistine ruler felt confident that David would remain his loyal servant for the rest of his life.
